translation: For a closed arithmetic sentence σ, Def2(σ) means that σ is true in the standard model of the natural numbers. For any set K of closed arithmetic sentences, Def3(K) means that for every closed arithmetic sentence σ, if σ belongs to K, then σ is true in the standard model; it imposes no condition on sentences outside K. For any such set K, Def4(K) means that no contradiction is derivable in classical first-order logic using K as the axiom set. K need not be deductively closed, and Def4 does not require that every member of K be true in the standard model.

divergences.description: The definitions apply to any set K of arithmetic sentences, not just the passage’s intended K of absolutely provable sentences. In particular, Def4 treats any such set as axioms, generalizing the consistency condition illustrated by PA.

judgement.summary: Def2 gives truth in the standard natural numbers, so taking T = {σ | Def2 σ} makes Def3 exactly K ⊆ T. Def4 gives the usual syntactic consistency condition: no contradiction is derivable.
